strictJson.method: Python json.loads with duplicate-key and invalid-constant rejection across formal data, schemas, and China JSON evidence

manualSchemaConformance.method: Read and enforced the actual Rolex catalog, market, and price-history schema constraints relevant to the China additions in a standalone script: required/no-extra top-level keys, marketCode/currencyCode/modelReference/configurationCode patterns, source/collectionAliases/localNicknames object shapes, and listingStatus/price combinations. Result: market file 1465/1465 watches unique and conformant; history file 1465/1465 price series conformant.

jsonSchema.reason: No installed Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validator was available (python jsonschema module and ajv-cli both absent); no dependency was installed without authorization.

crossFileConsistency.method: Ran the repository's cross-file invariant script (refPattern, watchCount, duplicate modelReference, market/history/catalog linkage, runId/price-status checks) scoped to rolex-china-market.json / data/history/CN, alongside the existing full-catalog checks; output: PASS: rolex-china-market.json.

websiteCompleteness.notes: The 1,872-result primary response included all 1,465 reported configurations. The subsequent firstResult=1465 response was empty. The rendered UI's own infinite scroll never advanced past its initial batch in this session (see collection-summary.json networkDiscovery.notes for the unrelated analytics-host DNS failure that caused this); this did not block completeness because the same structured endpoint the site itself uses was called directly and its terminal page was confirmed empty.

changeSafety.historyPreservation: CN is a new market with a single initial run; no prior CN run or price point existed to overwrite.

catalogReconciliation.notes: The China market data is entirely within the existing catalog union (C ∩ M = C = M). Per the single-market isolation rule, the catalog was not rewritten; only data/markets/rolex-china-market.json, data/history/CN/, and data/evidence/CN/ were added.

changeSafety.gitStatusScope: git status --short before and after this task showed only new, untracked paths under data/markets/rolex-china-market.json, data/history/CN/, and data/evidence/CN/; no existing tracked file was modified.

sensitiveDataScan.method: case-insensitive grep across all files under data/evidence/CN/2026-09-10/

taxRateVerification.verificationSource: Official Rolex China price notice ("已含增值税之参照零售价") cross-checked against the State Taxation Administration's (国家税务总局) published 13% standard VAT rate for goods under the VAT Law effective 2026-01-01.
taxRateVerification.limitation: China's additional import-stage consumption tax (消费税) on luxury watches is not separately itemized in Rolex's own price notice and is not captured by this schema's single taxRatePercent field; recorded as a limitation, not silently absorbed into the stored rate.

nicknameResearch.notes: See data/evidence/CN/2026-09-10/nickname-research.json for full detail. This is a representative, source-verified sample (4 exact-configuration nicknames across 3 model references, 2 family-wide aliases) rather than an exhaustive per-collection survey; the other 15 collections were left with empty names/sources rather than guessed.

independentSpotChecks.method: Called a second, separate official China API not used for the primary collection path: https://api.rolex.cn/api/prices/{rmc}?countryCode=CN&lang=zh-hans (per-model price microservice, response includes its own "currency":"CNY" field and VAT legal notice) together with https://api.rolex.cn/api/catalog/watches/{rmc}?language=zh-hans (per-model detail microservice, independently confirms case/dial/title text). Compared both against the primary watchgrid response for modelReference, price, and currency.

coverage.priceUnavailableCoverage: NOT APPLICABLE: all 1,465 structured records included a public price.
coverage.anomalyCoverage: NOT APPLICABLE: no duplicate, conflict, parse failure, or price-unavailable source record was observed.

readmeUpdate.reason: China increases covered markets from ten to eleven; its rolex.cn architecture (distinct domain, Coveo token endpoint alongside the same watchgrid pattern) and disclosed-VAT-only tax limitation are material enough to note alongside the market table.

limitations: No Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validator was installed, so generic JSON Schema validation is NOT RUN; strict JSON parsing and a direct implementation of the relevant schema constraints passed.

Chinese nickname research is a representative, source-verified sample (2 collectionAliases, 3 localNicknames across 4 configurations), not an exhaustive per-collection survey; the remaining 15 collections were left empty rather than guessed.

The stored 13% tax rate reflects only the VAT component Rolex's own price notice discloses; China's additional consumption tax on imported luxury watches, if embedded in consumer pricing, is not separately captured by this schema's single taxRatePercent field.

Catalog reconciliation (merging CN into data/catalog/rolex-catalog.json's sourceMarketCodes) was intentionally left to the coordinator per the multi-market isolation rule; this run confirmed the observed set is already a full subset/superset match (C ∩ M = C = M) but did not write to the catalog file.
